title: Beatrix and the Horizon
premise: Orsen Pemberton is a clone who inherited the original's unsolved murder case and a life spent hauling cargo through contested orbits, invisible by design. When a manifest for a ship that never flew lists a name he's never heard—his own original's true designation—he realizes someone is resurrecting the murder investigation from the other side. Racing a signal toward the relay at the edge of dead space, Orsen uncovers that the original was killed for discovering an inheritance fraud at the heart of the cloning consortium, and that the killer has been grooming Orsen as the perfect scapegoat all along. In the relay's cold heart, Orsen must choose between erasing his identity forever and broadcasting the truth, and he chooses broadcast—claiming the name Pemberton as his own, not his original's.
about_author: Sable Underhill is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent a decade writing shipping manifests before turning them into fiction. They live off-grid with two cats and a decommissioned navigation console they refuse to explain.

chapters.title: Dead Weight
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A routine cargo run through contested orbits establishes his careful invisibility: forged clearances, no questions, no history. He passes a checkpoint where a clerk lingers on his biometrics a beat too long. Emotional beat: the exhausting vigilance of a man who knows he's a copy of a dead man.

chapters.title: The Manifest That Never Was
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Docking at Meridian Station, he finds a ghost entry in the port registry: the freighter Calliope Vane, listed as destroyed five years ago, with a new outbound manifest bearing the name 'E. Pemberton—original.' His hands shake. Beat: dread disguised as curiosity.

chapters.title: Inherited Ghosts
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Orsen's POV. How clones inherit legal identity: the original's debts, warrants, and open murder case transferred to him at decanting. He never investigated who killed the first Pemberton. Beat: guilt over a death he remembers only as data.

chapters.title: The Clerk Who Lingered
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The checkpoint clerk, Ilsa Reyes, finds him in a dockside bar—not to arrest him but to warn him: someone paid for a full genealogical trace on Pemberton biometrics three days ago. Beat: paranoia crystallizing into purpose.

chapters.title: Calliope Vane
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. He breaks into the impound ring where the supposedly destroyed ship sits intact, scrubbed of registration. In the crew quarters: a second clone's growth tank, empty, its serial filed off. Beat: the horror of realizing he may not be the only copy.

chapters.title: Terms of Inheritance
chapters.summary: Introduces antagonist POV: Auditor Corvane of the Halcyon Cloning Consortium, reviewing Orsen's file like property. He authorized the trace. Beat: cold proprietary menace—we learn Orsen is an asset being recalled.

chapters.title: Running Dark
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. He strips the Calliope Vane's transponder codes and slips out of Meridian ahead of a Consortium detention order, taking Reyes along when her warning makes her a liability. Beat: reluctant alliance born of shared danger.

chapters.title: What the Original Knew
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. She decrypts fragments of the original Pemberton's sealed case file: evidence he'd found discrepancies in clone-lineage records—inheritances passing through clones to consolidate estates illegally. Beat: the murder case reframes as a cover-up.

chapters.title: Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A pirate toll station forces negotiation; Orsen trades spare parts for passage and learns the Consortium has posted a bounty describing him as 'escaped property,' not a person. Beat: dehumanization sharpening his resolve.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Reyes explains the target: Relay Kestrel-9, a dead-space listening post where the ghost manifest originated. Whoever sent it wanted someone to come. It's a trap or an invitation; either way, the signal is already traveling. Beat: commitment to the race.

chapters.title: Sable Water
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Resupply at a drifting colony ship; an old woman mistakes him for the original Pemberton and thanks him for something he never did—a debt forgiven, a kindness repaid to the wrong man. Beat: grief for a life he inherited but didn't live.

chapters.title: Corvane Closes
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. He dispatches a retrieval team led by Warden Tull, and we learn the scheme: frame the clone for the original's murder, close the case, bury the lineage fraud forever. Beat: the trap takes shape for the reader.

chapters.title: Tull
chapters.summary: Warden Tull's POV. A hunter who believes clones are property, tracking Orsen's fuel signature. Brief, chilling competence. Beat: the clock starts ticking audibly.

chapters.title: Two of a Kind
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Reyes finds genetic logs suggesting the empty growth tank held a third Pemberton—one decanted years earlier and unaccounted for. Is the ghost manifest sender the missing copy? Beat: identity fractures further.

chapters.title: The Dead Man's Ledger
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Hidden in the Calliope Vane's hull plating, the original's own cache: encrypted notes naming Consortium board members who used clone-succession to steal estates—including Corvane's own founding family. Beat: the inheritance theme turns literal and lethal.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Tull's ship ambushes them at a fuel depot; a brutal docking-bay fight leaves their cargo burned and Reyes wounded. They escape barely. Beat: first blood, real cost.

chapters.title: Field Medicine and Hard Truths
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV, feverish. While Orsen treats her wound, she asks the question he avoids: if the original died for this, what will the universe do with a copy who survives it? Beat: intimacy and doubt entwined.

chapters.title: The Signal's Origin
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Tracing the ghost manifest's routing, they find it bounced through Kestrel-9 but originated from inside Consortium headquarters. Someone internal is burning the house down. Beat: hope that an ally exists—possibly the missing clone.

chapters.title: Corvane's Confession Machine
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. We see him manufacture evidence pinning the original's murder on Orsen: fabricated logs, a coerced witness. The case that haunted Orsen since decanting is being weaponized. Beat: dramatic irony tightening the noose.

chapters.title: Dead Space
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The long silent transit toward Kestrel-9, systems failing, pursued. Orsen confesses to Reyes that part of him wants to erase himself rather than be anyone's inheritance. Beat: the darkest hour begins.

chapters.title: Kestrel-9
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. They reach the relay: ancient, half-dead, humming with stored transmissions. Inside, lights activate for them—the station was waiting. Beat: awe and terror at the threshold.

chapters.title: The Third Brother
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. In the relay's core: the missing clone, calling himself Anselm, the one who sent the manifest. He's spent five years assembling the fraud evidence and needed a Pemberton biometric to unlock the final archive. Beat: reunion with a self he never knew.

chapters.title: Three Names, One Face
chapters.summary: Anselm's POV. His account: decanted as a lab experiment, escaped, and dedicated to finishing the original's work. He doesn't trust Orsen—who lived soft while he suffered. Beat: friction between copies, identity as argument.

chapters.title: The Archive Locks
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The archive requires a living Pemberton's consent to open—and to broadcast. But consent also registers their location to every Consortium receiver. Opening it means dying in place. Beat: the choice made explicit.

chapters.title: Tull Arrives
chapters.summary: Tull's POV. The warden boards Kestrel-9 with a kill order, not a retrieval one—Corvane has decided dead evidence is best evidence. Beat: the law arrives as pure violence.

chapters.title: Siege in the Static
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Anselm seals the core; Reyes reroutes power; Tull's team cuts through bulkheads. A running battle through the relay's cathedral-like antenna halls. Beat: desperate, claustrophobic action.

chapters.title: What Justice Looks Like Out Here
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Wounded again, she confronts Tull directly, arguing the case no court will hear: the fraud, the murders, the personhood at stake. He hesitates—one heartbeat of doubt. Beat: justice argued outside the law.

chapters.title: Anselm's Sacrifice
chapters.summary: Anselm's POV. To buy transmission time, Anselm vents the core section with himself inside it, telling Orsen: 'Be the one who gets to be somebody.' Beat: devastating midpoint climax—brother dies so brother can speak.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. With Tull breaching, Orsen consents. The archive opens: lineage fraud, murder orders, Corvane's signature—all of it streaming toward every civil relay in range. Beat: triumphant, terrifying release.

chapters.title: The Fall of Corvane
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. The broadcast lands mid-board-meeting; allies scatter, warrants issue against him. He orders Tull to destroy the relay and everyone in it—last spite of a falling dynasty. Beat: villain unraveling.

chapters.title: Last Stand at the Antenna
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Final fight with Tull among the dishes. Orsen wins not by killing but by making Tull listen to the broadcast echoing overhead—the warden lowers his weapon as his own employer's crimes play out. Beat: victory without erasure.

chapters.title: Aftermath: The Case Closed
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Investigators arrive to find the original's murder solved by its own dead hand. Legally, Orsen inherits exoneration—an inheritance finally worth having. Beat: quiet catharsis.

chapters.title: Reyes's Report
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. She testifies, protects Orsen's status as a person not property, and chooses to stay with him rather than return to her old posting. Beat: chosen bonds over assigned ones.

chapters.title: The Name Question
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Offered a new identity, clean slate, any name he wants—he refuses. He'll keep Pemberton, but on his terms: the name now means what he did, not what was done to him. Beat: identity claimed, not inherited.

chapters.title: Consortium Reckoning
chapters.summary: Newsreel-style interlude, multiple brief POVs. Halcyon dissolves under indictment; clone-personhood cases flood every court; the phrase 'Pemberton consent' enters legal language. Beat: the world changing because one copy spoke.

chapters.title: Ghosts at the Dock
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. He visits the old woman's colony ship and returns the kindness properly, as himself. She still calls him by the original's name; he lets her, gently. Beat: peace with the inherited past.

chapters.title: The Empty Tank
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. He recovers Anselm's remains from the relay and gives him a burial in deep space, reading the original's ledger aloud—the work finished together. Beat: mourning a brother who was also himself.

chapters.title: New Manifest
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. He and Reyes refit the Calliope Vane, register it honestly under his true name, and take a contract hauling relief supplies to contested orbits—the routes he once ran scared, now run openly. Beat: transformation of the ordinary.

chapters.title: The Horizon Line
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A final message arrives from an unknown sender: another ghost manifest, another name. He smiles, files it, and plots the course. Beat: the vigilance remains, but now it's purpose, not fear.

chapters.title: Beatrix
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Orsen's POV. Revelation of the title: Beatrix was the original's name for the ship—and for the daughter whose stolen inheritance started everything; Orsen finds her alive, grown, and writes to her enclosing the restored estate. He signs it not 'E. Pemberton' but simply 'your father's echo, who finished the work.' Beat: inheritance redeemed across generations; the horizon finally reached.
